relevance_reason: Reports a patient with SCN caused by a homozygous loss-of-function CSF3 variant, the first confirmatory report of autosomal recessive CSF3-related SCN.

findings.statement: Almannai et al. (2026) reported severe congenital neutropenia caused by a homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in the CSF3 gene. They described this as the first confirmatory report of a previously proposed CSF3-related SCN, supporting the gene-disease relationship in humans.
quotes: We present the first confirmatory report of a previously proposed SCN due to a homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in CSF3.
Our report supports this new gene-disease relationship in humans.

variants.as_reported: homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in CSF3

relevance_reason: This paper first reports biallelic inactivating CSF3 variants in patients with severe congenital neutropenia, which defines SCN14.

findings.statement: Khouj et al. (2023) described 3 patients from 2 families with severe congenital neutropenia (SCN). Each family segregated a different biallelic inactivating variant in the CSF3 gene. Using skin fibroblast-derived RNA, RT-PCR showed complete deficiency of CSF3 caused by nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: Here, we describe three patients from two families each segregating a different biallelic inactivating variant in CSF3 with SCN.
Complete deficiency of CSF3 as a result of nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) could be demonstrated on RT-PCR using skin fibroblasts-derived RNA.

findings.statement: Khouj et al. (2023) suggested that CSF3 deficiency in humans causes a novel autosomal recessive form of SCN. Before this report, biallelic inactivation of the receptor gene CSF3R was an established cause of SCN, but no Mendelian disease had been ascribed to CSF3.
quotes: Our results suggest that CSF3 deficiency in humans causes a novel autosomal recessive form of SCN.
Although biallelic inactivation of its receptor CSF3R is a well-established cause of severe congenital neutropenia (SCN), no corresponding Mendelian disease has been ascribed to date to CSF3.

findings.statement: Khouj et al. (2023) noted that the phenotype in their patients with CSF3 deficiency mirrored the phenotype documented in mouse and zebrafish models of CSF3 deficiency.
quotes: The phenotype observed in this cohort mirrors that documented in mouse and zebrafish models of CSF3 deficiency.

relevance_reason: Mouse knockout of G-CSF (CSF3) giving chronic neutropenia; an animal model relevant to CSF3-related autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia.

findings.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) made G-CSF-deficient mice by targeted disruption of the G-CSF gene in embryonal stem cells. The G-CSF-/- mice were viable, fertile and superficially healthy but had chronic neutropenia, with peripheral blood neutrophil levels at 20 to 30% of wildtype. Heterozygous mice had intermediate neutrophil levels, which the authors suggested pointed to a gene-dosage effect. In G-CSF-/- marrow, granulopoietic precursor cells were reduced by 50%, and granulocyte, macrophage and blast progenitor cells were also reduced. Mature neutrophils were still present in blood and marrow.
quotes: G-CSF-deficient mice (genotype G-CSF-/-) are viable, fertile, and superficially healthy, but have a chronic neutropenia.

Peripheral blood neutrophil levels were 20% to 30% of wild-type mice (genotype G-CSF+/+) and mice heterozygous for the null mutation had intermediate neutrophil levels, suggesting a gene-dosage effect.
In the marrow of G-CSF-/- mice, granulopoietic precursor cells were reduced by 50% and there were reduced levels of granulocyte, macrophage, and blast progenitor cells.

phenotypes.text: reduced marrow granulocyte and macrophage progenitors

findings.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) found that G-CSF-/- mice had fewer neutrophils available for rapid mobilization into the circulation by a single dose of G-CSF. Giving G-CSF reversed the defect: 1 day of treatment brought circulating neutrophils up to normal levels, and after 4 days the marrows of knockout and wildtype mice looked morphologically indistinguishable.
quotes: G-CSF-/- mice had reduced numbers of neutrophils available for rapid mobilization into the circulation by a single dose of G-CSF.

One day of G-CSF administration to G-CSF-/- mice elevated circulating neutrophil levels to normal, and after 4 days of G-CSF administration, G-CSF+/+ and G-CSF-/- marrows were morphologically indistinguishable.

findings.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) showed that G-CSF-/- mice had a markedly impaired ability to control Listeria monocytogenes infection. Their blood neutrophil increase was diminished, their monocyte increase was delayed, and infection-driven granulopoiesis was reduced. The authors concluded that G-CSF is indispensable for maintaining normal steady-state neutrophil production, and they also implicated it in emergency granulopoiesis during infection.
quotes: G-CSF-/- mice had a markedly impaired ability to control infection with Listeria monocytogenes, with diminished neutrophil and delayed monocyte increases in the blood and reduced infection-driven granulopoiesis.
G-CSF is indispensible for maintaining the normal quantitative balance of neutrophil production during "steady-state" granulopoiesis in vivo
